messages.author: 839dfa09184985a5
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] time series distributions
parts:
Alright. Von mises won't be bad since the bessel functions are already
implemented. On the wiki for directional statistics, they mention a few
circular distributions, but some of them don't have a closed form (or
they require some weird function that I'm not sure we can implement
effectively) so it might be hard to implement. However, they have a
circular uniform that's just uniform from 0 to 2pi, von mises, and a
wrapped cauchy distribution that we may be able to implement efficiently.


- Peter

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] time series distributions
parts:
On 6/21/13 11:56 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> There is an ancient branch called circular where somebody implemented a couple of things.

I think the issue there was that we needed tests and doc.
The implementations looked OK to me the last time I looked.
So you should definitely start from there, Peter.

> As I recall, there was a
> question as to whether to go with the convention that the circular distributions be defined on (0,2 * pi) or (-pi,pi). I
> think it would be best to follow the conventions of the circular R package(s) whatever those are.

Here's the doc for circular:

http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/circular/circular.pdf

This package is hugely flexible and lets the user define
the units. e.g.,

x <- rvonmises(n=100, mu=circular(0), kappa=1)

where the circular() class is highly configurable. The default
is angle in radians, working modularly, so it's not constrained
to (0, 2*pi) or (-pi, pi) or whatever.

The nice part about working modulo 2*pi is that you get
2*pi == 0 instead of a discontinuity.

Even if we restrict the support of von_mises() to [0,2*pi),
we'll have an option to implement as:

parameters {
real<lower=0, upper=2 * pi()> theta;
}
model {
theta ~ von_mises(kappa);
}

or:

parameters {
real theta_raw;
}
transformed parameters {
real<lower=0,upper=2 * pi()> theta;
theta <- mod(theta_raw, 2 * pi());
}
model {
theta ~ von_mises(kappa);
}

Alternatively, we could have a new data type called "angle".
It could underlyingly be implemented one of the above two
ways.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] time series distributions
parts:
We can handle the uniform one already with a constrained
parameter.

I would suggest just doing the von Mises, since we've had
requests for that on the list. Given the vast number of distributions
out there that we could implement, I'd rather be driven by:


1. new research ideas we're working on,

2. concrete user requests for applied modeling problems, and

3. good demonstrations of what Stan can do.

So having one reasonable circular distribution is good for both (2)
and (3).

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: circular distribution mod 2 * pi ?
parts:
I think to match circular you want to evaluate the argument
as angle in radians modulo 2 * pi.

Is that OK with everyone else? It follows Ben's recommendation
to do what the R package circular does.

There's still the question of whether it would be better to
have an unconstrained varialbe that you took mod 2 * pi so that
it could circle around continuously rather than having 2 * pi
at the opposite end of a line from 0.

- Bob

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] circular distribution mod 2 * pi ?
parts:
I think it would be much better to have von_mises(kappa) defined on the whole line (mod 2pi) than restrict it's input to [0,2pi).  The (unconstrained) representation of real<lower=0,upper=2*pi> ends up (potentially) having an unnecessary multi-modality when the mode is anywhere near the end points.  This is going to make sampling much harder than it needs to be for no good reason that I can see.

Cheers,
Marcus
